title: Synthetic Business Cycle vs Shi-Xi-Xie's Germany.R method (West German reunification)
paper: Shi, Zhentao, Yishen Xi & Jin Xie (2025), "A Synthetic Business Cycle Approach to Counterfactual Analysis with Nonstationary Macroeconomic Data," arXiv:2505.22388; Section 5.1
reference_impl: Shi-Xi-Xie SBC method (Germany.R detrending + Synth::synth ipop, independent R run)
note: The deviation is the reference solver's, and it is in one place: the cyclical weight solve. The detrending and trend-forecast rows agree to 1.7e-14 of each series' scale (R's lm QR against numpy's lstsq). On the weight solve the program is strictly convex with a unique optimum, mlsynth attains it -- certified to 1.4e-6 by the convexity of the objective, and a cyclical sum of squares 2.6% lower than the authors' Synth::synth ipop reaches at any tolerance -- so the ATT and weight rows differ because the reference does not converge to the optimum. See docs/replications/sbc.rst.
